event.text: You can manage this yourself for now with over-the-counter allergy products — pharmacy-shelf antihistamines and nasal sprays are sold for these symptoms, and your pharmacist can help you pick one that fits your health history and other medicines. Follow the label instructions. If symptoms don't improve on an OTC medicine, contact a health care provider. If you develop trouble breathing, wheeze, or throat or face swelling, call 911 immediately. Hives alone, without those features, warrant a clinician's advice rather than emergency care.
